newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey may cut wheat import tax to 3 pct from 15.
newsitem.headline: Turkey may cut wheat import tax to 3 pct from 15.

text.p: Turkey is still working on a plan to reduce customs tax on wheat imports, possibly to three percent from 15, to make imports cheaper for its grain board and private millers, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said on Wednesday.
"To reduce the cost of imports the tax could be lowered to three percent. We are working on it," he told a news conference.
He did not say when the reduction would take place but indicated in a speech in parliament on Tuesday that the state grain board (TMO) might import an unspecified amount of milling wheat in December.
The TMO has been authorised by the government to import up to 500,000 tonnes to curb rising local wheat and bread prices, but no date for the imports has been given.
Asked when and how much would be imported, Demirci said: "We will import whenever necessary and at the required amount."

Wheat and bread prices have risen about 30 percent in the past three weeks after Turkey's crackdown on imported U.S. wheat due to ergot fungus, leading to the U.S. government's suspension of grain export certificates to Turkey.

Turkey was then enforcing a zero-tolerance limit for ergot in its Food Quarantine Act, but later backed down by raising the limit first to 0.02 percent and then to 0.05 percent after criticism from millers and U.S. officials.
Demirci said the TMO had begun selling wheat at cost in the local market to provide millers with cheaper wheat.
But millers, who depend largely on imported wheat to produce flour for export and domestic consumption, said the quality of local wheat was questionable and imports were inevitable.
Turkey has imported about 1.5 million tonnes so far in 1996 and the government has granted import licences for 3.2 million tonnes for imports until the end of the year.
Demirci said no U.S. wheat was being held at any port in Turkey and there was no intention to crack down on U.S. wheat.

"Any food item from the United States can enter Turkey as long as it meets the quality standards," he said. "We have never banned imports from the United States." --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara Newsroom, 90-312-4462940
